findings: Source is Rio Tinto H1 2026 interim results (29 July 2026, Investegate-style release), not slides-only; body text is substantial but truncated mid-Directors' Report (e36747cb4ebb850b.txt).

Group H1 2026 vs H1 2025: underlying EBITDA $14.8bn (+28% from $11.5bn); underlying earnings $6.9bn (+43% from $4.8bn); net earnings (PAT attributable) $6.7bn (+47% from $4.5bn); underlying EPS 421.4 US cents (+42% from 296.0); consolidated sales revenue $31.0bn (+15% from $26.9bn) (e36747cb4ebb850b.txt).

H1 2025 segment comparatives are labelled restated following the 27 August 2025 organisational restructure; Rio Tinto share of capital investment comparatives also restated after H2 2025 methodology change to include asset sales; free cash flow definition refined from H1 2026 to include Rio Tinto share of capital investment (e36747cb4ebb850b.txt).

Segment underlying EBITDA H1 2026 vs H1 2025 (restated): Copper $5.7bn (+84%); Iron Ore $6.8bn (-1%); Aluminium & Lithium $3.3bn (+38%); reportable segments total $15.8bn (+28%). Copper, Aluminium and Lithium collectively contributed >50% of group underlying EBITDA (e36747cb4ebb850b.txt).

Cash flow H1 2026 vs H1 2025: net cash from operating activities $9.2bn (+32% from $6.9bn); Rio Tinto share of capital investment $5.0bn (+12% from $4.5bn); free cash flow $3.8bn (+75% from $2.2bn); underlying EBITDA cash conversion 62% (+2pp). Working capital outflow $1.6bn; $443m Oyu Tolgoi tax payment (e36747cb4ebb850b.txt).

Balance sheet at 30 June 2026 vs 31 December 2025: net debt $14.1bn (-$0.3bn); cash and equivalents $9.1bn (from $9.2bn); net gearing 16% (from 18%); H1 net debt reduced $0.3bn after $4.2bn dividends paid (2025 final), capex and other flows (e36747cb4ebb850b.txt).

Interim ordinary dividend declared $3.4bn at 211 US cents per share (+43% YoY; 50% payout ratio). H1 cash dividends paid to equity shareholders $4.2bn (2025 final). Payment date 24 September 2026 (e36747cb4ebb850b.txt).

2026 production and sales guidance maintained (subject to weather impacts; Pilbara also subject to mining-area approvals and heritage clearances). Unit cost and share-of-capital-investment guidance maintained. Effective tax rate guidance lowered to ~25% from prior ~30% (expected ~30% from 2027). Copper C1 net unit cost range cut to US 30–50c/lb on 15 July (from US 65–75c/lb) due to higher gold prices and productivity (e36747cb4ebb850b.txt).

Weather/cyclone language: Q1 tropical cyclone ~8 Mt Pilbara weather-related impact with ~half expected recovered during 2026; productivity more than offset cyclone impacts; H1 2026 cyclone EBITDA impact less than H1 2025; bauxite ~0.9 Mt Q1 weather impact with ~half expected recovered. Overall production guidance held (not narrowed or cut), while copper unit-cost range was reduced separately on 15 July (e36747cb4ebb850b.txt).

Copper H1: production 442 kt (+1%); realised price 591 US c/lb (+35%); segment underlying EBITDA $5.7bn (+84%); C1 net unit costs -24.7 US c/lb. Oyu Tolgoi ramp-up; Kennecott/Escondida lower; Kennecott flash furnace breach late June—refined copper/gold lower in H2 but full-year copper including matte unchanged (e36747cb4ebb850b.txt).

Iron ore H1: Pilbara production 162.3 Mt (+6%) and shipments 157.7 Mt (+5%); highest H1 production since 2018; Pilbara realised price $92.6/dmt FOB (+2%). Simandou first sales April; H1 sales 0.4 Mt at 65.8% Fe; 2.2 Mt shipped to China; SimFer mine ~77% and port ~85% complete. IOC sales 6.5 Mt (-19%) (e36747cb4ebb850b.txt).

Aluminium & Lithium H1: underlying EBITDA $3.3bn (+38%); aluminium realised $4,343/t (+39%); LCE production 27.3 kt (+53% vs post-Arcadium H1 2025 comp); LCE realised $18,960/t (+22%). AP60 first hot metal March 2026; Boyne smelter secured A$2bn Queensland/Commonwealth package (March). Yarwun to cut alumina output 40% from October 2026 (e36747cb4ebb850b.txt).

Lithium/Rincon: first production at Fénix 1B and Sal de Vida ahead of plan in Q2; Rincon full-scale plant construction progressing toward ~200 ktpa LCE capacity by 2028; Rincon starter plant ramp-up focused on reactor stability (e36747cb4ebb850b.txt).
Glencore: preliminary combination discussions announced 9 January 2026; Rio Tinto ceased considering merger/combination 5 February 2026 (e36747cb4ebb850b.txt).
Tomago: not mentioned in this source body.
